boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten admission-free ways to share art, ideas, reading, and conversation on and near DePauw’s campus.

cards.entity_name: Richard E. Peeler Art Center Galleries
cards.title: Browse Peeler’s Rotating Exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Contemporary art without an admission charge
cards.notes: Meet in the Peeler lobby, explore its three galleries together, and check the exhibition calendar before university breaks.
cards.short_summary: A free gallery outing centered on DePauw’s changing contemporary-art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s gallery brochure states that all university exhibitions are free and open to the public and identifies three galleries inside the Peeler Art Center.
cards.access_notes: Open to the public; consult the current exhibitions page before visiting because galleries may close during university breaks and holidays.

cards.title: Explore Art at Emison
cards.subtitle: A second free exhibition stop on campus
cards.notes: Walk over with a friend and focus on one displayed object each; confirm current building access before setting out.
cards.short_summary: An admission-free companion to Peeler featuring works presented in the Emison Building.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s official gallery brochure identifies the Emison Galleries and states that all exhibitions at DePauw are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Public exhibition access is free; verify the current exhibition and building schedule before arrival.

cards.title: Schedule a Free Gallery Tour
cards.subtitle: A guided group activity for school or civic groups
cards.notes: Gather a school or civic group, then call or email Peeler staff in advance to arrange the complimentary guided visit.
cards.short_summary: A staff-guided way for eligible groups to discuss Peeler’s art without paying a tour fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peeler Art Center invites school and civic groups to schedule a free guided tour by telephone or email.
cards.access_notes: Advance scheduling is required; the free-tour offer is specifically documented for school and civic groups.

cards.title: See Express CAMP Art in the Great Room
cards.subtitle: Student-created art tied to ethical reflection
cards.notes: Check in at reception, pick up a visitor badge, and compare how the displayed works connect creativity with ethical questions.
cards.short_summary: A free public exhibit of student work inside the Prindle Institute’s Great Room.
cards.evidence_claim: The Prindle Institute says its Great Room displays Express CAMP student artwork and that all exhibits are free and open to the public during open hours.
cards.source_title: Our Campus - The Prindle Institute for Ethics
cards.access_notes: Visit during regular public hours, check in with staff in Room 104, and wear the provided visitor badge.

cards.title: Study the Prindle Foyer’s Rotating Art
cards.subtitle: Faculty and community work on public display
cards.notes: Start at the foyer after checking in, then choose one work to discuss before continuing through the institute’s exhibits.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost rotating display highlighting artwork by faculty and community contributors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Prindle Institute identifies rotating faculty and community artwork in the Prindle Foyer and states that all exhibits are free and public during open hours.
cards.source_title: Our Campus - The Prindle Institute for Ethics
cards.access_notes: Public access is available during institute open hours after reception check-in and use of a visitor badge.

cards.title: Walk the Cynthia O’Dell Photo Display
cards.subtitle: Nature Park photography along Prindle’s corridors
cards.notes: Follow the corridor display and compare the photographs with the surrounding Nature Park landscape visible outside.
cards.short_summary: A free indoor photo walk connecting documentary images with DePauw’s nearby natural setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Prindle’s official campus page says its corridors house the Cynthia O'Dell photography collection and that every exhibit is free and open to the public during open hours.
cards.source_title: Our Campus - The Prindle Institute for Ethics
cards.access_notes: Check in at reception during public hours, obtain a visitor badge, and remain within publicly accessible corridors.

cards.title: Share a Quiet Reading Hour
cards.subtitle: Ethics books in a public study space
cards.notes: Bring reading material or browse the ethics collection, keep conversation outside, and preserve the room’s designated quiet atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A contemplative public reading space for an intentionally quiet, purchase-free meetup.
cards.evidence_claim: The Prindle Institute says the Wood Library is open to the public during regular hours and that unreserved institute spaces are available for reading and study.
cards.source_title: Our Campus - The Prindle Institute for Ethics
cards.access_notes: Use during regular public hours, check in and wear a visitor badge; the Wood Library is reserved exclusively for quiet study.

cards.title: Talk or Play Yard Games in the Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Outdoor seating for informal gatherings
cards.notes: Choose the picnic-style seating for conversation or use the available yard games, while yielding any space already reserved.
cards.short_summary: An open-air social space supporting conversation and casual games without requiring a purchase.
cards.evidence_claim: Prindle describes its central courtyard as having picnic and discussion seating plus yard games, and says unreserved spaces are open to community members for discussion.
cards.source_title: Our Campus - The Prindle Institute for Ethics
cards.access_notes: Visit during public business hours, check in on arrival, and confirm the courtyard has not been reserved for another use.

cards.entity_name: Timothy and Sharon Ubben Lecture Series
cards.title: Attend an Ubben Lecture Together
cards.subtitle: Public talks by prominent visiting speakers
cards.notes: Check the series page for the next announced speaker, then review any free-ticket or registration instructions before attending.
cards.short_summary: A documented free public lecture series designed for shared learning and discussion.
cards.evidence_claim: DePauw’s official speakers page states that the Ubben Lecture Series is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Event dates and venues vary; consult the current series listing and follow any complimentary ticket or registration procedure.

cards.entity_name: James and Marilou Kelly Writers Series
cards.title: Hear a Kelly Writers Series Reading
cards.subtitle: Free author readings and literary discussion
cards.notes: Look up the current-season author and venue, read a short sample beforehand, and stay for the public discussion when offered.
cards.short_summary: A free literary gathering built around visiting poets, playwrights, and prose writers.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Kelly Writers Series page says the program brings writers to campus for readings and discussion and that all events are free and public.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current-season date, venue, and any registration instructions before attending; all series events are documented as free.
